brief.title: Business card: Maya Okafor, Product Designer
brief.brief:
Design a two-sided US business card (3.5 x 2 in) for Maya Okafor, Product Designer. Front: her name and title. Back: her contact details, email maya@example.com and website example.com/maya. Those are the only facts: do not add a phone number, address, company, social handles or anything else.

Deliver both sides as one self-contained HTML document (inline CSS and inline SVG only). On screen, show the front and the back as cards that scale fluidly to fit a phone and a desktop without sideways scrolling; you may add a short screen-only note beside the cards (not on them) stating the trim size and how to print. For print, add an @media print block with @page { size: 3.5in 2in; margin: 0 } so it prints as exactly two pages, page 1 the front and page 2 the back, each filling its page, with any screen-only notes hidden.

requirements.description: The front of the card shows the name "Maya Okafor" and the title "Product Designer".
The back of the card shows the email maya@example.com and the website example.com/maya.
Presents the card as two distinct sides, a front and a back.
Contains no invented contact details or facts: no phone number, address, company or social handles.

artifacts.title: Business card: Maya Okafor, Product Designer

render.note: KERNEL renders the watermarked preview (screen media only), exactly as for live entries.

judge.reason: The page meets all four requirements: correct front and back content, two distinct sides, and no invented details.

checks.reason: The front card shows the h1 'Maya Okafor' and the uppercase title 'Product Designer' beneath it, visible in both the desktop and phone screenshots.
The back card shows 'maya@example.com' with an EMAIL label and 'example.com/maya' with a WEBSITE label, both visible in the screenshots and linked.
The page presents two separate figure elements labelled FRONT and BACK, each a distinct card, and the print CSS sets a page break after the front so they print as two pages.
The visible content contains only the name, title, email and website; no phone number, address, company or social handles appear in the markup or screenshots.

narrative.overall_verdict: A clean, minimal two-sided card that uses only the supplied facts: a cream front with name and accent-coloured title, and a dark back with labelled email and website. It fits the 390px phone without sideways scroll.
strengths: Front uses a serif name with a small letterspaced accent title, giving a restrained, professional hierarchy.
Back's dark background with labelled EMAIL and WEBSITE rows reads clearly at both desktop and phone widths.
Print block sets @page to 3.5in x 2in with a page break between front and back, and hides the screen notes.
weaknesses: The small circular mark on the front is a generic decorative icon with no clear link to the brand.
The back's small caps labels are tiny and low contrast on the dark background at phone size.
Cards are presented on a plain beige page with no further context, so the layout is sparse on desktop.
narrative.best_for: best if you want a plain, understated card that uses only the name, title and two contact lines.

artifacts.title: Maya Okafor, Product Designer | Business Card

render.note: KERNEL renders the watermarked preview (screen media only), exactly as for live entries.

judge.reason: The submission meets all four requirements: both card sides show the supplied facts, present as two distinct sides, and add no invented contact details.

checks.reason: The front article shows the name 'Maya Okafor' (split over two lines as MAYA / OKAFOR in an h1) and the title 'Product Designer' in the accent colour, visible in the desktop and phone screenshots.
The back card shows 'Email' with maya@example.com and 'Website' with example.com/maya as links, visible in both screenshots.
Two separate article elements, a black front and an orange back, are presented as distinct cards, and the print CSS forces a page break after the front so each side prints on its own page.
The page contains only the name, title, email and website; the back-head 'Let's work together' is tagline copy, not a contact detail, and no phone, address, company or social handles appear.

narrative.overall_verdict: A clean, high-contrast two-sided card that shows the supplied name, title, email and website without invented details. The front and back are clearly separated, and the page lays out at phone width with no sideways overflow.
strengths: Bold black front with large uppercase MAYA OKAFOR and orange PRODUCT DESIGNER title gives clear hierarchy.
Back uses the accent orange with black contact labels, so email and website are easy to read.
Only the supplied facts appear; no phone, address or company were added.
weaknesses: The back adds a 'Let's work together' tagline that the brief did not supply; the buyer may want to remove it.
The orange mark on the front is a generic triangle with no link to the name, so it adds little identity.
On the phone the cards are fairly small, and the note text takes up a large share of the first screen.
narrative.best_for: best if you want a bold, minimal card with only your name, title and two contact lines
